claim: Response-level (macro) calibration does not imply atomic (per-claim) calibration -- a model can be well-calibrated overall while badly miscalibrated on individual factual claims within a long response.
stance_target: sufficiency of scalar/macro calibration metrics for structured outputs with multiple verifiable sub-units
scope_conditions: long-form NL generation, off-the-shelf LLMs, no additional training
quoted_support: it formalizes 'atomic calibration': decompose a long-form response x into atomic factual claims c_i..., and require P(y_i | f(c_i)=beta_i) = beta_i for every claim -- proves macro (response-level) calibration does NOT imply atomic calibration

claim: Existing LLMs exhibit poorer calibration at the atomic (per-claim) level than at the response (macro) level during long-form generation.
stance_target: the motivation for per-requirement/localized confidence over scalar confidence
scope_conditions: off-the-shelf LLMs, long-form generation benchmarks, general domain
quoted_support: LLMs exhibit poorer calibration at the atomic level during long-form generation

claim: Atomic Calibration is an analysis/benchmarking paper that studies existing LLMs' calibration properties rather than training models to become better calibrated, and taxonomizes confidence elicitation into discriminative (self-report) vs generative (external sample-consistency) methods, showing cross-category fusion beats same-category fusion.
stance_target: differentiation of Atomic Calibration's contribution type from DPRC's training-method contribution
scope_conditions: long-form NL factuality, evaluation methodology not training method
quoted_support: Atomic Calibration... is an ANALYSIS/BENCHMARKING paper, not a training method -- it studies existing off-the-shelf LLMs' calibration properties, it does not train models to become better calibrated.
